channel.title: Coastal Eventures: upcoming events
channel.description: The next 40 dated events on the Gulf Coast.

item.title: Game Days at Marina Bar & Grill (WED 10/7)
item.description: Thursday 10/1 | Marina Bar & Grill, Sandestin Golf and Beach Resort | No published price. Marina Bar & Grill at Baytowne Marina runs its own Game Days program, showing NCAA football on Saturdays and NFL games on Sundays plus select Monday and Thursday nights. It sits right on the marina at Sandestin.

item.title: Jazz Art Writers South Festival Youth Exhibit (WED 10/7)
item.description: Tuesday 9/15 | West Regional Library | No published price. West Regional Library hosts this youth exhibition tied to the Jazz Art Writers South Festival, a partnership between Mobile Arts Council and Amp Up Arts. More than 50 paintings by artists ages 8 to 18 line the space, each interpreting jazz through color and line. No viewing hours are published for Tuesday, September 15, so call the library to confirm.

item.title: Karaoke & DJ Nights: FUBAR Pizza Bar (WED 10/7)
item.description: Nightly · 9 PM-1 AM | FUBAR Pizza Bar | Free. Late-night karaoke runs five nights a week (Sun, Tue, Wed, Fri, Sat) plus a DJ on Monday and Thursday, 9 PM to 1 AM every night, with pizza till close. It is in Fort Walton Beach.

item.title: Karaoke Block: The Block (WED 10/7)
item.description: Wed-Sat · from 6 PM (Thu 8 PM) | The Block | Free. The Sports & Karaoke room at The Block runs Wednesday through Saturday, opening at 6 (8 on Thursday) and going late. It is downtown Fort Walton Beach.

item.title: Make It Last: Gallery Exhibition at UWF (WED 10/7)
item.description: Weekdays through 11/20 · 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM · opening reception Thursday 10/8 · 5:00 PM to 7:00 PM | UWF Center for Fine and Performing Arts, Building 82, The Art Gallery | Free. Make It Last is an exhibition in The Art Gallery at the UWF Center for Fine and Performing Arts, curated by a UWF graduate. Six artists share the space, which includes a conversation pit in the gallery alcove and a poetry wall that visitors fill with their own work. Admission is free, and the opening reception on October 8 runs from 5:00 PM to 7:00 PM.

item.title: Make Your Own Glass (hot glass, by appointment) (WED 10/7)
item.description: By appointment: Wednesdays 5 PM-9 PM, Saturdays 8 AM-11 AM | First City Art Center | from $85. Make Your Own Glass is a hands-on hot glass session at First City Art Center in Pensacola, where each participant makes a piece with a glassblower. It's for ages 8 and up including adults, by appointment on Wednesdays from 5-9 PM and Saturdays from 8-11 AM. The finished piece cools in an annealing oven and is picked up the following week. Standard pieces cost $85, and premium pieces such as a pumpkin, ornament, cup or bowl cost $110-$140.

item.title: MONOCHROME exhibition (WED 10/7)
item.description: Sunday 9/27 to Saturday 10/24 · times not posted | Blue Morning Gallery | No published price. Monochrome is a group show by three artists at Blue Morning Gallery, 21 S. Palafox Place in downtown Pensacola, running through Saturday, October 24. The black-and-white work asks what you notice, such as shadow angles, line curves and surface grain. The First Friday reception was October 2 and has passed.

item.title: Painting with a Twist Pensacola: paint-and-sip, family paint days and date nights (weekly programme) (WED 10/7)
item.description: Classes most days: family days Saturday 10:30 AM, brunch Sunday 11 AM, evenings Wednesday to Saturday | Painting with a Twist Pensacola | $35 per family. Painting with a Twist Pensacola is an artist-led paint-and-sip studio at 4771 Bayou Blvd Suite C11 with several classes every week. October has family paint days (ages 6 and up with a parent, no alcohol), adult Paint & Sip and Date Night classes (ages 16 and up on date nights), Halloween-themed canvases and Paint Your Pet. Classes cost $35-$60 depending on the class, and alcohol is sold on site with no BYOB.

item.title: Pensacola Beach Songwriters Festival (cherry-pick sets) (WED 10/7)
item.description: Oct 1-11 · venue-by-venue schedule | 22+ venues, Pensacola Beach + downtown | Free. Ten days of acoustic storyteller rounds run, mostly free, a build-your-own date. Many venues are bars; the cleaner picks are the daytime Gulfside Pavilion sets and restaurant listening rooms (Native Café, Flounders dinner sets).

item.title: Pensacola Beach Yoga: Friday and Wednesday beach classes (WED 10/7)
item.description: Fridays 9 AM and Wednesdays 6 PM | Pensacola Beach Yoga, beside the Gulf Pier | from $10. Pensacola Beach Yoga runs drop-in yoga on the sand beside the Gulf Pier at 41 Fort Pickens Road in Pensacola Beach. Classes are Fridays at 9 AM and Wednesdays at 6 PM, and they cost $10 with no registration. Bring a mat or towel.

item.title: Primal Fear Haunted Attraction at OWA (WED 10/7)
item.description: Select nights through October 31 · evenings | OWA Parks & Resort | No published price. OWA's immersive haunted attraction runs on select nights through the end of October, with dates including September 25 to 26 and October 2 to 3, 9 to 10, 16 to 17 and 19 to 31. A $7 Zombie Laser Tag add-on is available alongside the main attraction, and tickets are required.

item.title: The Boardwalk Columbus Day Weekend Celebration (WED 10/7)
item.description: Mon 10/5 to Sun 10/11 · see the daily schedule | The Boardwalk on Okaloosa Island | No published price. The Boardwalk on Okaloosa Island runs a week of Columbus Day programming from October 5 to October 11, new for 2026. The schedule is a pirate show on Monday from 5:30 PM to 8:00 PM, a movie on the beach on Tuesday at 8:00 PM, karaoke on Wednesday from 7:00 PM to 10:00 PM, and karaoke followed by a fireworks show on Sunday.

item.title: Wanda Sullivan: Bloem Exhibition (WED 10/7)
item.description: Now through December 11 | Anna Lamar Switzer Center for Visual Arts | No published price. A gallery exhibition by artist Wanda Sullivan runs at Pensacola State College's visual arts center through mid-December. The center's own site does not publish an admission price.

item.title: 2026 Navy Birthday Run (WED 10/7)
item.description: Wednesday 10/7 · 7:00 AM | Mustin Beach Club Trail Head, NAS Pensacola | Free. NAS Pensacola marks the Navy's birthday with a morning run from the Mustin Beach Club trail head at 7 AM on October 7. The run is free, and registered participants receive a free commemorative t-shirt, with registration through a Google form on the MWR page. Base access for the run is not specified, so settle that before you plan a morning around it.

item.title: 2026 ALA-CASE Fall Conference (WED 10/7)
item.description: Sunday 10/4 · 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM | Perdido Beach Resort | No published price. Perdido Beach Resort hosts the 2026 ALA-CASE Fall Conference on Sunday, October 4, from 8 AM to 5 PM. Alabama special education administrators and education leaders gather for professional learning across the day. The conference returns every year.

item.title: The Great Bellingrath Harvest (WED 10/7)
item.description: Daily through 11/8 · 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM | Bellingrath Gardens and Home | from $11. Bellingrath Gardens and Home runs a fall festival from September 19 through November 8 with seasonal displays across the gardens, including the scarecrow exhibit and pumpkin displays. The gardens are open daily, and the general admission price applies. The events page does not list a separate price for the harvest, so the gardens ticket is the number to plan with.

item.title: Shape & Sculpt Fitness Class (WED 10/7)
item.description: Wednesdays · 8:15 AM to 9:15 AM | Destin Community Center | from $5. Shape & Sculpt is a light-weight fitness class set to music at the Destin Community Center, built around muscle strength, balance and core work. The city says it's open to all ages and fitness levels, and it runs every Wednesday morning. Each class costs $5.

item.title: Billiards (WED 10/7)
item.description: 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM | Niceville Senior Center | from $5. Open-play billiards runs on the two pool tables at the Niceville Senior Center. City of Niceville residents get free membership, and everyone else pays a $5 day rate to play. The city says no experience is needed, so beginners and experienced players are equally welcome.

item.title: Café Social & Games (WED 10/7)
item.description: 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM | Niceville Senior Center | from $5. The Niceville Senior Center's 1950s-themed cafe hosts a casual social day with coffee and donated snacks. Members can settle into Rummikub, card games, puzzles, or dominoes at their own pace. City of Niceville residents get free access, and everyone else pays a $5 day rate.

item.title: Cornhole Open Play (WED 10/7)
item.description: 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM | Niceville Senior Center | from $5. Members toss bags at the boards during open-play cornhole at the Niceville Senior Center. It runs casually throughout the center's regular weekday hours. City of Niceville residents play free, and everyone else pays a $5 day rate.

item.title: Exercise Room (WED 10/7)
item.description: 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM | Niceville Senior Center | from $5. The Niceville Senior Center's exercise room stays open for members to work through strength, cardio, and flexibility routines on their own schedule. Equipment includes two recumbent bikes, a treadmill, free weights, a stability ball, mats, and stretch bands. City of Niceville residents get free access, and everyone else pays a $5 day rate.

item.title: Putting Green Open Play (WED 10/7)
item.description: 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM | Niceville Senior Center | from $5. Members check out putters and balls at the front desk to practice on the Niceville Senior Center's putting green. It is casual, and you can work on your short game alone or play a round with friends. City of Niceville residents get free access, and everyone else pays a $5 day rate.

item.title: Shuffleboard Open Play (WED 10/7)
item.description: 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM | Niceville Senior Center | No published price. Niceville Senior Center opens its shuffleboard courts to members age 55 and up for casual, all-skill-levels play throughout the day. The center frames it as relaxed social play with a little friendly competition, not a formal league. City of Niceville residents get free Senior Center membership. The open play session also repeats on weekdays through October.

item.title: Table Tennis Open Play (WED 10/7)
item.description: 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM | Niceville Senior Center | No published price. Niceville Senior Center's table tennis room is open for casual, drop-in play with no experience required. The city describes it as an active, social way to spend the morning rather than a competitive league. It shares the Tuesday 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM window with several other open-play programs at the center, and members age 55 and up are the intended audience.

item.title: Zumba Gold: Wednesday (WED 10/7)
item.description: Wednesdays · 8:30 AM to 9:30 AM | Niceville Senior Center | from $3. This Wednesday session of Zumba Gold is a low-impact class built around routines that are easy to follow. It asks a $3 donation and runs early, from 8:30 AM to 9:30 AM, at the Niceville Senior Center. It repeats weekly and is aimed at the center's members age 55 and up.

item.title: Adventure Zone at Steve's Fishing and Adventure Farm (WED 10/7)
item.description: Mon-Sat through Oct 31 · 9 AM to 6 PM | Steve's Fishing and Adventure Farm | No published price. Steve's Farm has rebranded as Steve's Fishing and Adventure Farm and opened a fall attraction in Walnut Hill with a corn maze, a giant slide, a kids' zipline, a jump pad, hayrides, a wagon train, a sunflower field and a pumpkin patch. It suits a family with small children who want a half day outdoors. The farm's own page does not print admission prices, so check the ticket page before driving out.

item.title: Indios Amigos: Traveling Exhibit at the Valparaiso Library (WED 10/7)
item.description: Mon 10/5 to Fri 10/9 · 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM | Valparaiso Library | No published price. The Valparaiso Library hosts Indios Amigos, a traveling exhibit made by the Florida Public Archaeology Network and the UWF Archaeology Institute, for Hispanic Heritage Month. The library says this is the only Okaloosa County stop for the exhibit, and it is open 9 AM to 5 PM through Friday, October 9. The listing is for families and everyone.

item.title: Veterans Chat 'n Chew (WED 10/7)
item.description: Wednesdays · 9:00 AM to 10:00 AM | Niceville Senior Center | from $5. Veterans gather at the Niceville Senior Center for an hour of casual conversation about the present and the past. The city describes it simply as a chance to get together with other veterans who share the experience. Access follows the center's usual membership rules, so residents attend free and others pay the standard day rate.

item.title: Beginner Line Dance: Wednesday (WED 10/7)
item.description: Wednesdays · 9:30 AM to 10:30 AM | Niceville Senior Center | No published price. This beginner line dance class teaches simple steps for members new to the form. Because the sessions run crowded, the city asks participants to pick either the Wednesday or the Friday class rather than attending both. It meets from 9:30 AM to 10:30 AM at the Niceville Senior Center and repeats weekly through October.

item.title: Ping Pong Meet-Up (WED 10/7)
item.description: 9:30 AM to 11:00 AM | Niceville Senior Center | No published price. This ping pong meetup at the Niceville Senior Center is open to beginners and experienced players alike, and the city says no experience is required to join in. It runs Wednesday mid morning and repeats on multiple weekdays.

item.title: Coco & Crawlers (WED 10/7)
item.description: Thursday 9/17 · 10:00 AM to 11:00 AM | Ben May Main Library, Youth Programming Room | No published price. This caregiver meetup in the Youth Programming Room at Ben May Main Library pairs children's play with a warm drink. It gives caregivers time to connect with each other. It runs Thursday morning from 10 AM to 11 AM, repeating on the third Thursday of the month, with more dates on October 15, November 19 and December 17. Registration is requested but not required.

item.title: Destin Fishing Rodeo: Daily Public Weigh-Ins (WED 10/7)
item.description: Daily, Oct 1 – Oct 31 · 10:00 AM-7:00 PM | Docks behind AJ's Seafood & Oyster Bar | Free. Anglers competing in the month-long Destin Fishing Rodeo bring their catches to the scale on the harbor docks behind AJ's Seafood & Oyster Bar every day in October. The public is welcome to watch for free from 10 AM to 7 PM, and the crowd tends to grow with the size of the fish coming off the boats.

item.title: Good Listener Storytime at Moorer (WED 10/7)
item.description: Wednesdays · 10:00 AM to 10:30 AM | Monte L. Moorer/Spring Hill Branch Library | No published price. Young children gather at the Monte L. Moorer/Spring Hill Branch Library for stories, songs and early literacy activities in this half-hour storytime. It is also offered again on Wednesdays, including October 7 and October 14.

item.title: Mexican Train Dominoes (WED 10/7)
item.description: 10:00 AM to 1:00 PM | Niceville Senior Center | No published price. Mexican Train Dominoes at the Niceville Senior Center is pitched as easy to learn, welcoming first-time players alongside the regulars. It runs Wednesday late morning into early afternoon and repeats on multiple weekdays.

item.title: Senior Social (WED 10/7)
item.description: Wednesday 10/7 · 10 AM to 11 AM | Gulf Breeze Library | Free. Adults 50 and older are invited to Gulf Breeze Library for Senior Social, an hour of coffee, conversation, arts and crafts, and games. The Friends of the Gulf Breeze Library provide refreshments. It runs one Wednesday morning a month, free to attend.

item.title: Shake, Rattle, & Read Storytime at West (WED 10/7)
item.description: 10:00 AM to 10:30 AM | West Regional Library | No published price. West Regional Library's Shake, Rattle, & Read Storytime pairs books with music and movement for young children and their caregivers. The library frames it as a chance for little ones to read, move, and build early literacy skills together. The library lists it every Wednesday and Thursday morning in the West Regional meeting room.

item.title: Table Tennis Open Play (WED 10/7)
item.description: 10:00 AM to 1:00 PM | Destin Community Center | from $2. Destin Community Center opens its tables for open table tennis play three days a week, Monday, Wednesday and Friday from 10 AM to 1 PM. Paddles and balls are provided, so nobody needs to bring their own equipment. Active Destin seniors play free, and non-residents pay $2.

item.title: Wonderful Wednesday Storytime at Theodore (WED 10/7)
item.description: Wednesdays · 10:00 AM | Theodore Oaks Branch Library | No published price. Theodore Oaks Branch Library's Wonderful Wednesday Storytime introduces young children to books, rhymes and music in the children's area. The program is built for preschoolers up to age 5, though all ages are welcome. Space is limited and seats go first come, first served.

item.title: Senior Bible Study at Midway Baptist Church (WED 10/7)
item.description: Wednesdays through October 28 · 10:10 AM to 11:30 AM | Midway Baptist Church | No published price. A weekday-morning Bible study for seniors runs every Wednesday at Midway Baptist Church, ahead of the same building's Wednesday-night Awana club for kids. The church's calendar names the group and the hour and does not post a price. Call ahead if the group's format or study material matters to you before you go.

item.title: Good Listeners Storytime at Semmes (WED 10/7)
item.description: Wednesdays · 10:30 AM to 11:00 AM | Semmes Regional Library | No published price. Semmes Regional Library runs a half hour storytime built around stories, songs, movement and a craft, aimed at building early literacy and social skills in young children. It repeats every Wednesday, so a missed week is never the only chance.
